note.explanation: An element’s formula shows how that element exists: as single atoms or as molecules. A compound’s formula shows the atoms or ions in it and their ratio. For covalent compounds, the molecular formula shows the kinds and numbers of atoms in one molecule. For ionic compounds, the formula unit gives the minimum ratio of the ions.
examples: O₂ is the formula of an element that exists as molecules: one molecule contains two oxygen atoms.
NaCl is the formula unit of an ionic compound: sodium ions and chloride ions are present in a 1:1 ratio.
note.checkAnswer: O₃ is an elemental molecule with three oxygen atoms in each molecule.
note.simple: A chemical formula is a short way to show which atoms or ions are present and how many of each there are.
note.checkQuestion: What does O₃ tell you about one molecule of ozone?
note.title: Reading chemical formulae
steps: Check whether the formula represents an element or a compound.
For an elemental molecule, read the subscript as the number of atoms in one molecule.
For a covalent compound, read the subscripts as the numbers of atoms in one molecule.
For an ionic compound, read the formula as the simplest ratio of its ions.
note.answer: O₃ shows that one molecule of ozone contains three oxygen atoms.

mcqs.stem: Which formula represents an element shown by its symbol alone?
rationales: Na represents sodium as an element shown by its symbol alone.
O₂ represents an element whose atoms are bonded in a molecule.
H₂O is a compound containing hydrogen and oxygen.
O₃ is a molecule of the element oxygen, not its symbol alone.

mcqs.stem: How many oxygen atoms are in one molecule of O₂?
rationales: O₂ has a subscript 2, so it contains two oxygen atoms.
The subscript 2 means there are two oxygen atoms in one molecule.
Three oxygen atoms would be written O₃.
Four oxygen atoms would be written O₄.

options: One hydrogen atom and one oxygen atom
Two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom
One hydrogen atom and two oxygen atoms
Two hydrogen atoms and two oxygen atoms
mcqs.stem: What does the molecular formula H₂O show about one molecule of water?
rationales: H₂ has a subscript 2, so water has two hydrogen atoms, not one.
H₂ means two hydrogen atoms and O with no subscript means one oxygen atom.
O has no subscript, so there is one oxygen atom, not two.
The formula has no subscript 2 after O, so it does not show two oxygen atoms.

options: The mass ratio of the ions
The minimum ratio of the ions
The number of molecules in a crystal
The number of atoms in an element
mcqs.stem: What does the formula unit of an ionic compound show?
rationales: A formula unit describes the ratio of ions, not their mass ratio.
It shows the minimum ratio present between the ions.
A formula unit does not state the number of molecules in a crystal.
This describes neither the ionic ratio nor a formula unit.

mcqs.stem: Which formula shows calcium and chloride ions in the simplest 1:2 ratio?
rationales: CaCl shows a 1:1 ratio, not 1:2.
CaCl₂ shows one calcium for every two chlorine atoms.
Ca₂Cl shows a 2:1 ratio, not 1:2.
Ca₂Cl₂ reduces to a 1:1 ratio, not 1:2.

mcqs.stem: Which formula represents a covalent compound that exists as discrete molecules?
rationales: NH₃ is ammonia, a covalent compound represented by molecules.
NaCl is an ionic compound represented by a formula unit.
CaCl₂ is an ionic compound represented by a formula unit.
KBr is an ionic compound represented by a formula unit.

written.text: How would you differentiate between the chemical formula of an element and that of a compound? Give examples.
written.finalAnswer: An element’s formula represents one kind of atom, such as Na or O₂. A compound’s formula represents two or more kinds of atoms or ions in a fixed ratio, such as H₂O or NaCl.

rubric.why: The answer must identify that an element contains only one kind of atom.
rubric.description: State what an element’s formula represents.
rubric.how: Say that it represents one kind of atom and give an example such as Na or O₂.

rubric.why: The answer must distinguish a compound from an element.
rubric.description: State what a compound’s formula represents.
rubric.how: Say that it represents two or more kinds of atoms or ions.

rubric.why: A formula communicates the relative numbers of the particles present.
rubric.description: Explain what the subscripts or formula unit indicate.
rubric.how: Mention the fixed number or ratio of atoms or ions.

rubric.why: Relevant examples show the distinction clearly.
rubric.description: Give suitable examples of an element and a compound.
rubric.how: Include an elemental formula and a compound formula.

modelAnswer: An element’s formula represents one kind of atom; for example, Na or O₂.
A compound’s formula represents two or more kinds of atoms or ions in a fixed ratio; for example, H₂O or NaCl.

written.text: Write down the names of ionic and covalent compounds whose formulas have been given in this article.
written.finalAnswer: Ionic compounds: sodium chloride (NaCl), calcium chloride (CaCl₂), potassium bromide (KBr) and barium chloride (BaCl₂). Covalent compounds: hydrogen chloride (HCl), hydrogen fluoride (HF), hydrogen sulfide (H₂S), phosphine (PH₃), hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂), sulfuric acid (H₂SO₄), carbon dioxide (CO₂), carbon monoxide (CO), benzene (C₆H₆), water (H₂O), ammonia (NH₃) and methane (CH₄).

rubric.why: Correct identification of the ionic examples earns credit.
rubric.description: Name ionic compounds from the article.
rubric.how: Give the names of the ionic compounds and match them to their formulae.

rubric.why: The other ionic examples must also be recognised.
rubric.description: Name the remaining ionic compounds.
rubric.how: Include potassium bromide and barium chloride.

rubric.why: These are examples of covalent compounds listed in the article.
rubric.description: Give covalent compound names.
rubric.how: Name at least the listed hydrogen compounds correctly.

rubric.why: Correct names distinguish two different covalent formulae.
rubric.description: Name the carbon oxides.
rubric.how: Identify CO₂ as carbon dioxide and CO as carbon monoxide.

rubric.why: These familiar molecular compounds are also named in the section.
rubric.description: Include the other named molecular compounds.
rubric.how: Give the names water, ammonia and methane.

modelAnswer: Ionic compounds: NaCl is sodium chloride; CaCl₂ is calcium chloride; KBr is potassium bromide; BaCl₂ is barium chloride.
Covalent compounds: HCl is hydrogen chloride; HF is hydrogen fluoride; H₂S is hydrogen sulfide; PH₃ is phosphine.
H₂O₂ is hydrogen peroxide; H₂SO₄ is sulfuric acid; CO₂ is carbon dioxide; CO is carbon monoxide; C₆H₆ is benzene.
H₂O is water; NH₃ is ammonia; CH₄ is methane.

written.text: Write down the chemical formula of barium nitride.

rubric.why: The formula must use the correct symbols and balance the ion charges.
rubric.description: Show the correctly balanced barium and nitride ratio.
rubric.how: Combine Ba²⁺ and N³⁻ so the total positive and negative charges cancel.

rubric.why: The final formula is the required answer.
rubric.description: Write the simplest neutral formula unit.
rubric.how: Write Ba₃N₂.

modelAnswer: Barium ion = Ba²⁺ and nitride ion = N³⁻.
The simplest ratio that balances the charges is 3 Ba²⁺ : 2 N³⁻.
Formula = Ba₃N₂.

written.text: Write down the chemical formulas of the following compounds. Calcium phosphate, Aluminium nitride, Sodium acetate, Ammonium carbonate and Bismuth sulphate.
written.finalAnswer: Calcium phosphate: Ca₃(PO₄)₂; aluminium nitride: AlN; sodium acetate: CH₃COONa; ammonium carbonate: (NH₄)₂CO₃; bismuth sulphate: Bi₂(SO₄)₃.

rubric.why: The first two formulae require the correct ions and ratios.
rubric.description: Give the formulae of calcium phosphate and aluminium nitride.
rubric.how: Write Ca₃(PO₄)₂ and AlN.

rubric.why: The acetate formula must have the correct composition.
rubric.description: Give the formula of sodium acetate.
rubric.how: Write CH₃COONa or an equivalent formula.

rubric.why: The ammonium ions must balance the carbonate ion.
rubric.description: Give the formula of ammonium carbonate.
rubric.how: Write (NH₄)₂CO₃.

rubric.why: The bismuth and sulfate ions must be in the correct neutral ratio.
rubric.description: Give the formula of bismuth sulphate.
rubric.how: Write Bi₂(SO₄)₃.

rubric.why: The final set must contain all five correct formulae.
rubric.description: Check and present the complete set.
rubric.how: Ensure all five formulae are correct and use parentheses for repeated polyatomic ions.

modelAnswer: Calcium phosphate: Ca²⁺ and PO₄³⁻ give Ca₃(PO₄)₂.
Aluminium nitride: Al³⁺ and N³⁻ give AlN.
Sodium acetate: Na⁺ and CH₃COO⁻ give CH₃COONa.
Ammonium carbonate: NH₄⁺ and CO₃²⁻ give (NH₄)₂CO₃.
Bismuth sulphate: Bi³⁺ and SO₄²⁻ give Bi₂(SO₄)₃.

written.text: Different compounds will never have the same molecule formula but they can have the same empirical formula. Explain
written.finalAnswer: The statement is not always correct: different compounds can have the same molecular formula, as structural isomers do. They can also have the same empirical formula; for example, ethene (C₂H₄) and propene (C₃H₆) both have the empirical formula CH₂.

rubric.why: A scientifically accurate answer should not repeat the incorrect absolute claim.
rubric.description: Address whether the statement is universally true.
rubric.how: Explain that different compounds can share a molecular formula.

rubric.why: An example supports the distinction between formula and structure.
rubric.description: Give an example of compounds with a shared molecular formula.
rubric.how: Name structural isomers such as ethanol and dimethyl ether, both C₂H₆O.

rubric.why: The empirical formula expresses the simplest atom ratio.
rubric.description: Explain why different compounds can share an empirical formula.
rubric.how: State that different molecular formulae can reduce to the same simplest ratio.

rubric.why: A valid example demonstrates the shared empirical formula.
rubric.description: Give compounds with the same empirical formula.
rubric.how: Use ethene and propene, which both reduce to CH₂.

modelAnswer: The statement is not always correct because different compounds can have the same molecular formula if their atoms are arranged differently.
For example, ethanol and dimethyl ether are different compounds with the molecular formula C₂H₆O.
Different compounds can also have the same empirical formula, which is the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms.
For example, C₂H₄ and C₃H₆ both reduce to the empirical formula CH₂.

written.text: The chemical formula for sand is SiO₂ but the sand does not exist in the form of discrete molecules like H₂O. How has its formula been determined keeping in view its structure?
written.finalAnswer: Sand is a giant network solid, not a collection of separate SiO₂ molecules. Its formula SiO₂ shows the simplest 1:2 ratio of silicon atoms to oxygen atoms in the structure.

rubric.why: The answer must recognise that sand is not made of separate molecules.
rubric.description: Describe the structure of sand.
rubric.how: State that it has an extended network structure rather than discrete molecules.

rubric.why: The formula contains silicon and oxygen.
rubric.description: Identify the elements present.
rubric.how: Name silicon and oxygen.

rubric.why: The formula expresses the ratio of atoms in the network.
rubric.description: State the atom ratio represented by the formula.
rubric.how: Give the silicon-to-oxygen ratio as 1:2.

rubric.why: The final formula must match the stated simplest ratio.
rubric.description: Write the formula representing the ratio.
rubric.how: Write SiO₂.

modelAnswer: Sand has an extended network structure and does not consist of separate SiO₂ molecules.
Its structure contains silicon and oxygen atoms in a 1:2 ratio.
The formula shows the simplest ratio of atoms in the solid.
Therefore, the formula is SiO₂.

examTips: Short questions may ask you to write a formula, name a compound, or distinguish an element’s formula from a compound’s formula.
For ionic formulae, show the simplest ratio that makes the total positive and negative charges balance.
In explanations, state what the subscripts mean; for example, H₂O contains two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom in each molecule.
Use the term formula unit for ionic compounds and molecular formula for covalent compounds that exist as molecules.
The last line of a formula question should clearly show the correct formula, with subscripts and brackets placed correctly.

hints: Identify the charges on barium and nitride ions.
Choose the smallest number of each ion that makes the total charge zero.
yourTurn.question: Write down the chemical formula of barium nitride.
solution: Barium ion = Ba²⁺ and nitride ion = N³⁻.
The lowest common total charge is 6: three Ba²⁺ ions give +6 and two N³⁻ ions give −6.
The simplest ratio is 3 Ba²⁺ : 2 N³⁻.

hints: Sand is not made of separate SiO₂ molecules.
Read SiO₂ as a simplest atom ratio: one silicon atom for every two oxygen atoms.
yourTurn.question: The chemical formula for sand is SiO₂ but the sand does not exist in the form of discrete molecules like H₂O. How has its formula been determined keeping in view its structure?
solution: Sand has an extended network structure, not separate SiO₂ molecules.
The atoms in this structure are present in a silicon-to-oxygen ratio of 1:2.
The formula gives the simplest ratio of atoms in the structure.
yourTurn.answer: SiO₂ represents the simplest 1:2 ratio of silicon to oxygen atoms in sand’s network structure.

steps.why: The formula H₂O is the molecular formula of water given in the section.
The subscript 2 applies to hydrogen, so there are two hydrogen atoms.
steps.text: Count the hydrogen atoms: H₂ means two hydrogen atoms.

steps.why: O has no subscript, so one oxygen atom is present.
steps.text: Count the oxygen atoms: O means one oxygen atom.

steps.why: The molecular formula tells us which atoms and how many are bonded in one molecule.
steps.text: One molecule of water contains two hydrogen atoms bonded to one oxygen atom.

example.question: What does the chemical formula H₂O show about one molecule of water?
example.answer: One molecule of water contains two hydrogen atoms bonded to one oxygen atom.

explain.title: Elements can have different formula forms
explain.body: Some elements are represented by their symbols alone, such as Na, Ca, C and Fe. Other elements exist as molecules, such as O₂, N₂ and H₂. O₃ is ozone: each molecule contains three oxygen atoms.

explain.title: Ionic compounds use formula units
explain.body: In an ionic solid such as sodium chloride, oppositely charged ions form a crystal. Its formula unit shows the minimum ratio of the ions. NaCl has a 1:1 ratio; CaCl₂ has a 1:2 ratio of calcium to chlorine.

explain.title: Covalent compounds have molecular formulae
explain.body: Covalent compounds generally exist as molecules. The textbook defines a molecular formula this way: “A chemical compound is thus, represented by a chemical formula which is called the molecular formula of that compound and which shows all the types of atoms bonded together in one molecule of that compound.” For example, H₂O shows two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom in one molecule.

explain.title: Read subscripts carefully
explain.body: A small number after a symbol tells you how many of that atom are present. No subscript means one. In NH₃ there is one nitrogen atom and three hydrogen atoms.

explain.title: Formula and structure are not always the same thing
explain.body: A formula can show the simplest ratio in an ionic or extended solid without meaning that separate molecules exist. For example, SiO₂ represents the 1:2 ratio of silicon to oxygen in sand’s structure.

mistakes: Treating an ionic formula unit as if it described a separate molecule.
Forgetting that an element can exist as a molecule, such as O₂, rather than as single atoms.
Reading a missing subscript as zero; no subscript means one atom.
Changing a polyatomic ion’s subscripts instead of putting brackets around the ion, for example writing NH₄₂CO₃ instead of (NH₄)₂CO₃.
Writing a formula with charges that do not balance, or not reducing the ion ratio to the simplest whole numbers.
Assuming that every different compound must have a different molecular formula; structural isomers can share one.
